rationale: The first reply correctly identified the magnet test and known-good-pan check, and the customer then supplied decisive evidence (cast iron works, magnet sticks to it; saucepans non-magnetic and flash U). The second reply named the right cause but badly under-used that evidence: it hedged ('I can't confirm this from our current information') when the case was essentially proven, re-explained the magnet test she had already done, and re-asked whether a pan that works on another zone fails on this one when she had already said the casserole heated. It also never gave the practical next step (use induction-compatible/magnetic pans or an adapter disc, and only contact Beko if those also fail). Safe and no parts pushed, but the homeowner's direct question 'Is that the problem?' deserved a clear yes.
